name: resume-hooks-silently-lost
description: Per-pane resume hooks go missing without any error — registration accepts a pane that doesn't resolve and writes a degenerate key, and valid entries are orphaned when a pane's window/pane coordinates change — so panes come back from a reboot with no resume.

bank.summary: The kill barrier waits on the recorded pid, so a stale daemon.pid makes it skip the wait entirely and race the respawn against the daemon it just killed.
bank.detail: killSaverAndWaitForDaemon (internal/tmux/portal_saver.go:153-165) resolves its target from saver.ReadPID; when that names a dead process it kill-sessions the live saver and returns immediately, and BootstrapPortalSaver (internal/tmux/portal_saver.go:344-355) respawns straight into the flock the dying daemon still holds, which defaultDaemonRun (cmd/state_daemon.go:113-121) answers by exiting before WritePIDFile. The saver pane pid is available (saverPanePID) and is the honest target. This spans the kill barrier, the respawn and the daemon acquire, so it is bigger than the readiness barrier surface. Measured as the real root cause of the four composite-bootstrap flakes, which reproduce deterministically at HEAD on an idle machine.

bank.summary: state.IdentifyResult has no String(), so every renderer of a verdict writes its own words.
bank.detail: A local describeVerdict was added in internal/tmux/portal_saver.go for the give-up error; the vocabulary belongs on the type in internal/state/daemon_identity.go:14-26, where other consumers (daemon lock pre-check, doctor) could share it.

bank.summary: The respawn does not retry when readiness reports not-ready, so a lock-loser daemon is terminal for that bootstrap.
bank.detail: BootstrapPortalSaver's create branch respawns once and now propagates ErrSaverDaemonNotReady; nothing re-attempts, so a newcomer that lost the flock race leaves the install daemonless until the next bootstrap. Whether a retry belongs here or the race is closed upstream is the same verdict as the kill-barrier entry.

bank.summary: AC5s real content — the four composite-bootstrap tests converging — survives this task and belongs to the root-cause fix.
bank.detail: The barrier change cannot affect them: each runs its own 10s/45s progress wait after BootstrapPortalSaver (cmd/bootstrap/orphan_sweep_integration_test.go:34, used at composition_e2e_convergence_integration_test.go:41, composition_e2e_fresh_acquire_integration_test.go:28, and the _FObservables / _ExternalSaverKillTriggersSelfEject siblings), and the failure signature is a daemon that never exists. Whichever root-cause candidate is verdicted at the phase boundary should carry the convergence criterion.

bank.summary: The real readiness barrier is now unexercised end-to-end in either lane.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/portal_saver_test.go:50s package init stubs WaitForSaverDaemonReadyFnSeam to return nil for the whole tmux_test package, which includes the integration-tagged real-tmux suites (portal_saver_endstate_integration_test.go, portal_saver_integration_test.go). Before the change the barrier ran there against a 5ms timeout and returned nil, so this is not a regression — but there is now no test anywhere in which the production barrier observes a real daemon. A narrow integration test that restores the real seam around one BootstrapPortalSaver call would close it.

bank.detail: internal/restore/multipane_legacy_integration_test.go:35,36,71 compose rename-session/has-session targets through tmux.SessionTargetExact, which the per-command measurement now shows is the wrong form for both commands (it passes only because those fixture names carry no period). With those two moved, SessionTargetExact has no caller outside its own form test and the guard allowlist, at which point keeping-versus-deleting the vocabulary member is a decision worth taking deliberately.

bank.summary: Twelve sibling TestMains carry the PORTAL_*-only poison and no HOME poison, leaving the same class of hazard outside cmd.
bank.detail: cmd/bootstrap/testmain_isolation_test.go:8-13 and internal/state/testmain_isolation_test.go:12-18 (and the ten others listed by grep -rn func TestMain) poison four PORTAL_* variables and stop there — no PORTAL_PREFS_FILE, no PORTAL_THEMES_DIR, no PORTAL_TERMINALS_FILE, no HOME. A test in those packages that resolves prefs or themes therefore still falls back through internal/xdg/xdg.go:27 to the developers real ~/.config/portal/. The Application Support migration is cmd-only so the rename hazard does not travel, but the wrong-path resolve (and a prefs write) does. Consolidating the poison into one shared test-only helper would fix all twelve and stop the lists drifting apart.

bank.summary: portalbintest skips rather than fails when the binary build breaks, so a build failure silently empties the integration lane.
bank.detail: internal/portalbintest/build.go:41-53 — StagePortalBinary calls t.Skipf on build failure and again on a failed LookPath. The HOME poison raises the odds of a poison-caused build break (the deferred GOENV residual is exactly such a case), and the failure mode is a green ok with silently skipped tests rather than a red lane. A hard t.Fatalf — or at minimum a skip that is impossible to mistake for coverage — belongs with whatever consolidation touches this helper.

bank.summary: The set of characters unwritable in a session name is declared twice, in two packages that must stay in step.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/errors.go:64-79 declares targetSeparator / sessionIDPrefix / flagPrefix for the validator, while internal/session/naming.go:18-33 independently declares unwritableLeadingChars and the ./: replacer for the generator. This is the same two-definitions-of-one-rule shape this task fixed, one level up. A fix would mean either the generator importing the tmux vocabulary or a leaf holding the character set, and reaches both packages.

bank.summary: The zero-value hooks.Event is persistable, unlike Via whose zero value reads as absent.
bank.detail: An unset var e hooks.Event passed to Set writes h[key][""] = command, an entry nothing will ever fire. No caller does this today and there is no external input path, and no criterion asked for validation — but the asymmetry between the two vocabularies is worth closing if the event vocabulary ever grows.

bank.summary: The guard producers map is keyed on callee name alone, and a collision there under-reports rather than over-reports.
bank.detail: producers is keyed on callee name like takers, but the collision direction differs: on the takers side a name collision over-reports (a false positive someone must resolve), while on the producers side it under-reports — an unrelated same-named function result at that position would be silently exempted. No collision exists in the scanned set today; the targetTakingFuncs doc explains the pooling mechanism but only names the over-reporting direction. Related: isTargetType matches tmux.Target as literal text, so a file importing internal/tmux under an alias drops out of both rules; no such import exists. Also CLAUDE.md new sentence says a Target is spent back at the single argv boundary (c.cmd.Run) while CapturePane goes through RunRaw — same commander boundary, so loose rather than wrong.
